title: Influence of the dosage form and the patient-specific dosage on acceptance and the complexity of using oral dexamethasone in children and Adolescents as part of antiemetic prophylaxis during chemotherapy
summary:
In order to avoid nausea and vomiting, medication is given as a precautionary measure during chemotherapy.
This standard includes the active ingredient dexamethasone, which is swallowed as a tablet. This active ingredient is known to have a bitter taste. In addition, the dose of this medication is calculated individually for each child based on height and weight. This means that different strengths of tablets often have to be combined and/or tablets have to be halved or quartered. 
It is possible to prepare the required dose of dexamethasone for each child in the hospital pharmacy in the form of a single tablet. For this purpose, a new technology - so-called 3D printing - is used, with which it is possible to produce a tablet that is easy for children to swallow and at the same time masks the bitter taste of the active ingredient. 
It is not yet known which of the two possible types of medication is more pleasant to swallow and less complicated.
conditions: Antiemetic prophylaxis in the context of chemotherapy

interventions.name:
In addition to their indicated chemotherapy, patients also receive dexamethasone as prophylaxis against nausea
- During a cycle of chemotherapy in the form of commercial tablets (dosage if necessary by dividing and/or combining different strengths)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Pediatric patients aged six and over who are treated in the Clinic for Pediatric Hematology and Oncology at the University Hospital Hamburg-Eppendorf
2. Indication for at least two cycles of dexamethasone-containing antiemetic prophylaxis in a solid oral dosage form during chemotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
1. Lack of written consent from patients and/or legal representatives
2. Lack of ability to participate in the survey (linguistic, cognitive)
